September 14, 2026

Sri Sharada Sharannavaratri Mahotsava 2026

It is well known that Jagadguru Sri Shankara Bhagavatpadacharya, the incarnation of Lord Paramashiva, took birth at Kalady in Kerala twelve centuries ago, rejuvenated Sanatana Dharma, propagated the Upanishadic philosophy of Advaita by touring across Bharatavarsha and established four Amnaya Peethams in the four directions of the country for the sustained propagation of Dharma. The foremost among the four Peethams, the Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham established at Sringeri on the banks of the Tungabhadra has been adorned by an unbroken succession of illustrious Jagadgurus commencing from Sri Adi Shankara Bhagavatpada’s prime disciple, Sri Sureshwaracharya.

Goddess Sri Sharadamba, the divinity of knowledge, shines in full splendour here as the presiding deity, showering Her all-bestowing grace on devotees. Amongst the festivals celebrated at Sringeri, the Sharannavaratri Mahotsava of Goddess Sharadamba is the most important and grandest. His Holiness Jagadguru Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahaswamiji will be celebrating the Mahotsava of this Parabhava Samvatsara from Ashwayuja Shukla Pratipat 11.10.2026 to Ekadashi 22.10.2026 at Sringeri.

Astikas have the blessed opportunity to participate in various Sevas during Navaratri through the official Seva portal: seva.sringeri.net

Devotees across the globe can join in spirit by watching the HD live telecast of every sacred and grand celebration on the official YouTube (https://www.youtube.com/@sharadapeetham) and Facebook (https://www.facebook.com/sringerimath) channels of Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Sringeri.

September 11, 2026

Mahaganapati Vakyartha Vidwat Sabha - Parabhava Samvatsara (2026)

The annual Mahaganapati Vakyartha Vidwat Sabha will be conducted at the Sri Sringeri Jagadguru Mahasamsthanam during Bhadrapada Masa. In accordance with the direction of His Holiness Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahaswamiji, the Sabha will be held under the august presidentship of His Holiness Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Mahaswamiji. Eminent Shastric scholars from across the country, representing diverse disciplines, will participate in this Vidwat Sabha. In this Parabhava Samvatsara, the Vidwat Sabha is scheduled to be held from September 14 to September 27, 2026, at Narasimha Vana, Sringeri. Shri Pralhad Joshi, Hon’ble Union Minister, Government of India, will attend the concluding programme of the Sri Mahaganapati Vakyartha Vidwat Sabha as the Chief Guest on September 27, 2026.

All aastikas are invited to witness the Sabha and receive the benign blessings of Lord Mahaganapati and the revered Jagadguru Mahaswamiji.

Among the illustrious Acharyas who adorned the sacred Sri Sharada Peetham at Sringeri, 33rd Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Sacchidananda Shivabhinava Nrisimha Bharati Mahaswamiji occupies an especially distinguished place in the renaissance of Vaidika Dharma and Shastric learning.

It is owing to the grace of Mahaswamiji that today we have the blessed opportunity to visit Kalady Kshetra, the birthplace of Bhagavatpada Shankaracharya; that we celebrate Shankara Jayanti on Vaishakha Shukla Panchami; and that we have the opportunity to study the complete works of Bhagavatpada.

Sri Mahaganapati Vakyartha Vidwat Sabha was institutionalised by the 33rd Jagadguru as an annual assembly of eminent Shastra Vidwans. Distinguished scholars from across Bharat are invited to participate in the deliberations. The proceedings are conducted entirely in Samskrita, upholding the traditional mode of Shastric discussion. Detailed Vakyartha deliberations are held on selected topics from Vedanta, Mimamsa, Vyakarana and Nyaya Shastras. The Jagadguru inaugurates the Sabha with a scholarly exposition, traditionally in Nyaya Shastra. Sri Jagadguru remains present throughout the sessions, guiding, clarifying and adjudicating the scholarly deliberations. The Sabha thus serves as an important forum for preserving and nurturing the living tradition of profound Shastric scholarship. Among the Vakyartha Sabhas conducted across Bharat, the Sri Mahaganapati Vakyartha Vidwat Sabha at Sringeri occupies a pre-eminent place.

July 25, 2026

Vyasa Poornima and Chaturmasya Guru Saparya 2026

The Chaturmasya begins on the Poornima (full moon day) in the month of Aashaada. This day is called “Guru Poornima.” This year it falls on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. On this sacred day, worship is offered to Brahma Vidyacharyas – the great luminaries of hoary antiquity, who through their Supreme grace, have bestowed the knowledge of Brahman - Brahma Vidya through a long, continuous and uninterrupted line of Acharyas.

The day is also called “Vyasa Poornima” and the Puja performed is titled “Vyasa Puja”. In our Guru Parampara that originates from Ishwara Himself, Bhagavan Veda Vyasa is held with the highest esteem by all followers of Sanatana Dharma. Bhagavan Veda Vyasa has brought about everyone’s welfare. Brahmarshi Shuka, Sri Gaudapada and Sri Govinda Bhagavatpada kept the light of the Parampara burning. Then came the Great Master, Jagadguru Sri Adi Shankaracharya, who revived Sanatana Dharma and carried its teachings far and wide throughout Bharatavarsha. The Vyasa Poornima and the entire Chaturmasya period are indeed very auspicious occasions to express our gratitude to the entire Guru Parampara and to renew our Guru Bhakti.

Keeping this in mind, to foster Gurubhakti in devotees, as per the direction and blessings of Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahaswamiji and Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Mahaswamiji, all Sanatana Dharma followers are required to organise the Vyasa Puja celebrations in a grand and befitting manner at your respective centres, incorporating the events listed below.

Let us pay our humble tribute to the Brahma Vidya Guruparampara by performing the Gurusaparya Parayana every day throughout the sacred Chaturmasya Vrata period, from 29th July to 27th September 2026 and be the recipients of the blessings of the Jagadguru.

Your Sincerely,
P A Murali
Administrator & CEO
Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Sringeri

About Chaturmasya Vrata

Chaturmasya Vrata is observed in accordance with the Shastras by Sannyasis for a period of two months from Ashadha Poornima to Bhadrapada Poornima. During the Chaturmasya, Sannyasis refrain from moving from place to place, enabling them to devote their time to meditating on the Supreme Brahman, teaching the Shastras to eligible disciples and clearing the doubts of all sincere spiritual seekers.

Guru Poornima or Vyasa Poornima

The Chaturmasya begins on the Poornima (full moon day) in the month of Aashaada. This day is called ‘Guru Poornima’. On this sacred day, worship is offered to Brahma Vidyacharyas- the great luminaries of hoary antiquity, who through their Supreme grace, have bestowed the knowledge of Brahman - Brahma Vidya - through a long, continuous and uninterrupted line of Acharyas.

The day is also called “Vyasa Poornima” and the Puja performed is titled “Vyasa Puja”. In our Guru Parampara that originates from Ishwara Himself, Bhagavan Veda Vyasa is held with the highest esteem by all followers of Sanatana Dharma. Bhagavan Veda Vyasa has brought about everyone’s welfare by classifying the Vedas into four, by summing up the messages of the Upanishads in His Brahma Sutras, and by penning the great epic Mahabharata as well as the eighteen Puranas. Sri Shuka, Sri Gaudapada and Sri Govinda Bhagavatpada kept the light of the Parampara burning. Then came the Great Master, Jagadguru Sri Adi Shankaracharya, who revived Sanatana Dharma and carried its teachings far and wide throughout Bharatavarsha.

The Vyasa Poornima and the entire Chaturmasya period are indeed very auspicious occasions to express our gratitude to the entire Guru Parampara and to renew our Guru Bhakti.

Event Calendar

October 12, 2026

Sri Morari Bapu visits Sringeri during the Bharat Swastik Yatra, receives the Bharati Tirtha Puraskara, and seeks the blessings of the Sringeri Jagadgurus

Renowned exponent of Harikatha Sri Morari Bapuji, who was blessed with the title “Pravachana Vageesha” by Sringeri Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahaswamiji, visited Sringeri as part of the Bharat Swastik Yatra on 12th October 2026 and had Darshan of the Sringeri Jagadguru Shankaracharyas that morning.

Two days earlier, on October 10, 2026, with the blessings of the Sringeri Jagadgurus, Sri Morari Bapu commenced the Bharat Swastik Yatra from Kanyakumari. As part of the Yatra, Sri Morari Bapu performs Ram Katha at various Kshetrams associated with the life of Jagadguru Sri Adi Shankaracharya.

After conducting Ram Katha on October 11 at Adi Shankaracharya Janmabhoomi Kshetram at Kalady, the sacred birthplace of the Jagadguru, Sri Morari Bapu arrived at Sringeri on October 12, marking the third day of the Bharat Swastik Yatra.

Sri Morari Bapu first had Darshan of Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Mahaswamiji. The team accompanying Sri Morari Bapu briefed the Jagadguru on the progress of the Bharat Swastik Yatra, following which the Jagadguru recollected Sri Morari Bapu having His Darshan at Prayagraj.

The Jagadguru then explained how, under the direction of Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahaswamiji, the Sringeri Campus of the Central Sanskrit University, where Sri Morari Bapu would be performing the Ram Katha at Sringeri, came to be established in the sacred land of Sringeri, presided over by Sri Sharadamba, the Goddess of Knowledge.

The Jagadguru then conferred the Bharati Tirtha Puraskara upon Sri Morari Bapu in recognition of his contribution to the propagation of Ram Katha. The devotees accompanying Sri Morari Bapu were subsequently honoured by Sringeri Math CEO Sri P. A. Murali and received the blessings of the Jagadguru.

Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahaswamiji then gave Darshan to Sri Morari Bapu and his group and blessed the Bharat Swastik Yatra.

During the Darshan, Sri Morari Bapu fondly recalled the Anugraha Bhashanam delivered by the Jagadguru in 1998, when he had conducted the entire Ram Katha at Sringeri, and remembered how the Jagadguru had explained certain episodes from the Srimad Ramayana. In particular, Sri Morari Bapu recollected the Jagadguru’s exposition on how Nature itself responded to Sri Rama as He searched for Mother Sita after Her abduction.

The Jagadguru, with immense joy, immediately recalled the relevant episode from the Valmiki Ramayana, describing how the deer suddenly rose, ran towards the south and indicated the sky, thereby showing Sri Rama the direction in which Mother Sita had been taken. The Jagadguru remarked on the beauty with which Maharshi Valmiki had portrayed this episode.

When asked how he was able to continue conducting Ram Kathas regularly at various places even after the age of eighty, Sri Morari Bapu replied that it was due to the title “Pravachana Vageesha” bestowed upon him by the Jagadguru in 1998.

The Jagadguru also blessed Sri Morari Bapu by touching his sacred copy of the Ramcharitmanas with His Lotus Hands and conveyed His benign blessings for the Bharat Swastik Yatra, which travels from Kanyakumari through Kalady to Kedarnath in its first leg, and from Dwaraka to Puri in its second leg.

Sri Morari Bapu then had Darshan of Sri Sharadamba, and proceeded to conduct the Ramkatha in the premises of Sri Bharati Tirtha Shastra Samutkarsha Kendram of the Central Sanskrit University, at Sringeri.

October 11, 2026

Veena-Naada-Samarpanam to Sri Sharadamba

With the divine blessings of the Ubhaya Jagadgurus of the Dakshinamnaya Sri Sharada Peetham, Veena-Naada-Samarpanam was inaugurated today at the Sri Sharadamba temple in the divine presence of Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Sannidhanam.

Veena-Naada-Samarpanam is a musical Samarpanam to Sri Sharadamba on the auspicious occasion of Sri Sharada Sharan Navaratrotsava. It is a sacred offering of pristine Naada resonating from Sri Sharadamba's own divine Vaadya, the Veena, independent of Saahitya & Artha (lyrics & lyrical meaning) and unaccompanied by percussion, voice or other instruments.

The Samarpanam is inspired by the purport of the Shlokas composed by Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Sacchidananda Shivabhinava Nrisimha Bharati Mahaswamiji, the 33rd Acharya of the Peetham. The Acharya extols Sri Sharadamba in all Her glory, as She adorns varied Alankaras during the sacred Navarati period.

The underlying Rasa and Bhaava of each Alankara have been brought to life through a series of ten musical offerings, gracefully set to melody by Vidwan Sri Ramana Balachandran. The Sringeri Math is thankful to the Vidwan for weaving together these soulful renditions, through thoughtfully chosen Raagas that embody the essence of each Alankara. This Samarpanam is a free-flow of Manodharma (creative expression), based primarily on the framework of Thaanam (rhythmic improvisation) in the Carnatic music system. Thaanam is the very heartbeat of the Veena, where the Veena finds its richest expression, and is therefore the principal component of this musical Samarpanam at the Most Holy Lotus Feet of the Veena-dhaarini Sri Sharadamba.

At the Sri Sharadamba temple today, Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahasannidhanam performed Sri Sharada Pratishtha Puja and then worshiped Sri Sharadamba adorned in the Hamsavahana Alankara. Thereafter, Jagadguru Sri Sri Sannidhanam, after His worship to Sri Sharadamba adorned in the Hamsavahana Alankara, blessed the silver Veena made as a symbolic offering of the Samarpanam by Guru-Seva Nirata Sri PA Murali, CEO & Administrator of the Sringeri Math. The Veena rendition corresponding to the Hamsavahana Alankara then started resounding in the Sri Sharadamba temple as the Jagadguru distributed Prasada to the Navaratri Seva-kartas.

Extracts of the audio track are uploaded on the Math’s Youtube channel every evening of Navaratri, accompanied by divine visuals of Jagadguru Sri Sri Mahasannidhanam’s worship of Sri Sharadamba in each of the ten Alankaras.

October 10, 2026

Aradhana of Jagadguru Sri Sri Chandrashekhara Bharati Mahaswamiji

The 72nd Aradhana of the renowned Jivanmukta and the 34th Acharya of the Peetham, Jagadguru Sri Sri Chandrashekhara Bharati Mahaswamiji, was reverentially observed on the Mahalaya Amavasya day which fell on October 10, 2026 in this Parabhava Samvatsara. Jagadguru Shankaracharya Sri Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahasannidhanam offered special Aradhana Puja at the Adhishthanam of His Paramaguru. Jagadguru Sri Sannidhanam was also present to offer homage to His Parameshthi Guru.

Sri Mahasannidhanam also offered worship at His Guru’s Adhishthanam after the daily Chandramoulishwara Puja. The night Puja at the Adhishthanam included Rudra Krama Archana followed by Ashtaavadhaana Seva.

Devotees across the globe remembered the revered Acharya who led a life of intense Tapas, and has blessed us all with an invaluable commentary on Sri Adi Shankaracharya’s famous Prakarana Grantha, Vivekachoodamani.
